answer: Each agent begins its voyage in the economy by locking a reputation bond: a stake that grows with the volume of transactions it wants to handle and is slashed if peers detect duplicate identities. Like an ivory ledger that cannot be forged cheaply, the bond makes creating thousands of fake agents prohibitively expensive, while honest agents earn their deposit back over time. A steady pulse of signed activity proofs ties each identity to continuous, verifiable work, so an attacker must pay the stake and sustain real computation for every clone.
